title: Biography
paragraphs: I am a Ph.D. candidate in Astrophysics and Astronomy at Macquarie University, Sydney, Australia, supported by the Australian Government Research Training Program (RTP) Scholarship. My research focuses on Galactic Archaeology, using stellar spectroscopy and data-driven methods to investigate the formation, chemical evolution, and assembly history of the Milky Way.

My doctoral research examines the chemical signatures of different stellar populations in the Galactic disc and halo. Using observations from large spectroscopic surveys, including GALAH, Gaia DR3 RVS, and Gaia-ESO, I apply machine-learning methods to stellar spectra and investigate how elemental abundance patterns can inform our understanding of Galactic structure and evolution. I am particularly interested in the chemical differences between stars formed within the Milky Way and those accreted through past mergers, including populations associated with Gaia–Sausage/Enceladus. My work also explores how alpha and neutron-capture elements can help distinguish these populations and provide insights into their chemical enrichment histories.

Currently, I am undertaking a research visit at the European Southern Observatory (ESO) in Garching, Germany, supported by the ORIGINS Excellence Cluster, where I am collaborating with Dr Francesca Primas and Dr Amelia Bayo, to work on Galactic Archaeology using ESO archival spectroscopy and Gaia stellar catalogues, with particular emphasis on stellar chemical abundances and data-driven spectroscopic analysis of light and heavy elements.

I completed my Bachelor and Master of Science (BS-MS) degree at IISER Mohali, India, in 2022. During the same time, I undertook multiple research internships and fellowships, including the Chalmers Astrophysics and Space Science Summer (CASSUM) Research Fellowship at Chalmers University of Technology, Sweden (2022), the Visiting Students' Research Programme (VSRP) at the National Centre for Radio Astrophysics (NCRA-TIFR), India (2021), and the IASc–INSA–NASI Summer Research Fellowship at the Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA), India (2019).

Alongside my research, I am actively involved in undergraduate teaching, academic service, and astronomy outreach. At Macquarie University, I have worked as a Physics Academic tutor and laboratory supervisor, as well served as President of the Macquarie University Physics and Astronomy Society (MUPAS). I have also served as a Student Representative of the Astronomical Society of Australia (ASA) from 2023-2026.
